headline: Homebuilders and Consumer Names Lead a Broad Thursday Rally as Chip-Adjacent Stocks Drag
body_html:
Thursday's session is shaping up as a convincingly positive one across most of the market, with 362 names in our 544-stock universe trading higher against 180 that are lower. Homebuilders are the day's runaway sector leader, up roughly 3.9%, followed by consumer stocks gaining more than 3.1%. Software and healthcare are also comfortably in the green, while materials and industrials are making modest progress.

The dominant theme mid-session is a rotation toward rate-sensitive and consumer-facing names, aided by a slide in Treasury yields as buyers moved into bonds. That bond bid appears to be partly a safety reflex tied to geopolitical turbulence in the Gulf, where renewed Houthi threats against Saudi Arabia have unsettled regional markets. The contrast is stark on the other side of the ledger: semiconductors are off 1.56% and energy is down 1.14%, acting as the primary drags.

Winnebago Industries and Thor Industries are the standout movers, each surging more than 8% and underscoring the surprisingly strong bid for recreational-vehicle and consumer-discretionary names. Into the close, watch whether that yield decline holds and whether the semiconductor pressure deepens or stabilizes.

briefs.headline: RV Makers Surge in Tandem on Consumer Optimism
briefs.body: Winnebago Industries and Thor Industries are each up more than 8% mid-session, making them the two strongest performers in our universe today. The paired move suggests fresh conviction that the consumer-spending outlook is firming, particularly for big-ticket discretionary purchases. Neither company has issued fresh guidance, pointing to a sentiment-driven bid.

briefs.headline: Treasury Yields Retreat as Bond Buyers Seek Safety
briefs.body: Investors are rotating into U.S. government bonds Thursday, pulling yields meaningfully lower and providing a tailwind for rate-sensitive sectors including homebuilders and software. The safety bid appears linked at least in part to escalating Houthi threats against Saudi Arabian targets, which rattled Gulf equity markets overnight and kept risk appetite cautious globally.

briefs.headline: Houthi Pressure on Gulf Markets Ripples Into U.S. Session
briefs.body: Renewed warnings from Yemen's Houthi movement to strike Saudi Arabia again have unsettled Gulf bourses and contributed to a cautious tone in energy and geopolitically exposed names. The development is also prompting broader diplomatic strain, with the European Union and Gulf states postponing a scheduled summit that had been set to take place in Saudi Arabia.

briefs.headline: Vicor Tumbles More Than 11%, Leads a Sharp Tech-Power Selloff
briefs.body: Vicor Corporation is the session's worst performer, sliding 11.58%, with the pain spreading across semiconductor-adjacent hardware names. FormFactor, Advanced Energy, Keysight, and Semtech are each down between 6% and 7.3%, collectively pressuring the semiconductors sector to a loss of roughly 1.6% — the worst sector reading of the day.

briefs.headline: Cboe Set to Extend Options Trading Hours for Key Securities
briefs.body: Exchange operator Cboe is moving to expand the hours during which options on major stocks and ETFs can be traded, a structural shift that could increase after-hours hedging activity. The change would give institutional and retail participants more flexibility to manage risk around earnings releases and breaking macro events outside standard session hours.

briefs.headline: AppFolio and Trade Desk Post Strong Gains, Lift Software Sector
briefs.body: Property-technology software firm AppFolio is up 7.15% and advertising-technology platform Trade Desk has gained nearly 7%, helping push the broader software sector to a 2.06% advance. The moves suggest selective enthusiasm for high-growth software names even as investors rotate more aggressively into economically sensitive consumer and homebuilder stocks today.
